analysis: Report all three endpoints and costs without choosing a winner from a single seed and short training horizon. History, parameter sharing and FLOP differences are explicit confounds; the matched-history and equal-compute follow-ups remain separate experiments.

cnn.information: Last 8 six-plane observations, history-presence indicators, and action/previous-pass planes strictly preceding each observation.

transformer.information: Complete causal visual observation/action history, up to 512 positions; nine soft observation patches per 9x9 board.

budget.repair_policy: Keep every failed attempt. Freeze and record a source repair before a retry; do not retune from held-out scores.

controls: Same immutable dataset and complete-episode partitions
Same 128 sequences per pod update, 64 expert and 64 behavior
Same per-rank episode, bucket, and D4 RNG seeds
Same optimizer, LR schedule, gradient clipping and three supervised objective weights
No auxiliary exit loss in either arm
128 updates from independently initialized models; checkpoint at 128; validation at 0,64,128; full test at final

endpoints.go_strength: A fresh, separately registered paired KataGo match panel is required; offline losses alone cannot qualify playing strength.
systems: Total pod reservation chip-hours including compilation, evaluation and checkpointing
Compiler FLOP estimates with stated limitations

question: Does a near-parameter-matched conventional residual CNN learn the same weak-teacher corpus more effectively in a short controlled offline screen?
